newsitem.title: USA: Neose begins Phase II anti-ulcer trials.
newsitem.headline: Neose begins Phase II anti-ulcer trials.

text.p: Neose Technologies Inc said Tuesday that it has started a Phase II clinical trial of NE-0080, an orally administered carbohydrate drug being developed for the prevention and treatment of H. pylori.
H. pylori is the bacterium responsible for most cases of gastritis and ulcers.

"Once this Phase II trial is completed, we plan to initiate a larger Phase II study later this year. Our Phase I trial demonstrated that NE-0080 was well-tolerated, and showed evidence of anti-bacterial activity," the company said in a press release.

The primary objective of this initial, placebo-controlled, Phase II trial is to evaluate the safety, tolerance, and pharmacokinetics of multiple, oral doses of NE-0080 in asymptomatic, H. pylori-positive male volunteers.
Twenty- one volunteers will receive 1, 2, or 5 grams of NE-0080 four times per day for up to 56 days.
H. pylori load will be measured using the urea breath test, a non-invasive assay that measures the enzyme urease, a specific H. pylori marker, and endoscopic exam.
The company said it hopes to use the dosing protocols determined in this initial Phase II study in subsequent clinical studies that will utilize larger numbers of symptomatic patients.

The company said that in ongoing preclinical studies with a monkey model for human H. pylori infection, NE-0080 showed the ability unequivocally to eradicate the bacteria from stomachs, as demonstrated by histological examination and by culture of endoscopic biopsies.
